# Multi-Agent and Trustworthy AI Laboratory: Recruitment

> Official public recruitment page of the Multi-Agent and Trustworthy AI Laboratory, Faculty of Information Technology, University of Science, VNU-HCM (FIT, HCMUS).

## About the Laboratory

- **Institution:** Faculty of Information Technology, University of Science, Vietnam National University Ho Chi Minh City (FIT, HCMUS).
- **Head of Lab:** Prof. Long Tran-Thanh (Professor, University of Warwick, UK).
- **Faculty Mentors:** Assoc. Prof. Nguyen Van Vu, Dr. Chau Thanh Duc, Dr. Le Trung Hoang.
- **Student Team:** 5 undergraduate researchers at FIT, HCMUS.
- **Current Opening:** Recruiting 5 undergraduate students (year 1 to year 4).
- **Work Mode:** Mostly online, scheduled around classes, with a weekly lab meeting and a weekly 1-on-1 with a mentor.
- **Compute Resources:** Projects that need GPUs get access to the lab's GPU servers.

## Core Research Pillars

1. **Multi-Agent Systems & Game-Theoretic AI:** Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL), algorithmic game theory, strategic coordination, negotiation, and LLM-based agent societies. Target venues: NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, AAMAS.
2. **Culture-Aware & Trustworthy Foundation Model Alignment:** Aligning large language and vision-language models with diverse cultural, ethical, and safety norms. Topics include steering black-box models via APIs and defending against jailbreaks. Target venues: NeurIPS, ICML, ACL, EMNLP, TACL.
3. **Continual Learning & Reliable Computer Vision:** Mitigating catastrophic forgetting in open-world settings, online learning algorithms, and reliable visual recognition under real-world distribution shifts. Target venues: NeurIPS, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV.

## Key Publications and International Recognition

- **Training-Free Cultural Alignment of Large Language Models via Persona Disagreement** (NeurIPS 2026 Main Track, [arXiv:2605.10843](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10843)).
- **Weather-Robust Cross-View Geo-Localization via Prototype-Based Semantic Part Discovery** (NeurIPS 2026 Main Track, [arXiv:2605.11654](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11654)).
- **Payoff Scaling Shapes Cooperation in LLM Agents Across Languages** (Royal Society Interface Focus, [arXiv:2601.19082](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.19082)).
- **The Mouse vs. AI Robust Foraging Competition** (1st Place Champion across both tracks, NeurIPS 2025 Competition Track; Team HCMUS_TheFangs, technical report [arXiv:2602.00982](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.00982), competition page: [NeurIPS 2025 Competition](https://neurips.cc/virtual/2025/competition/127735)).
- **Unlocking Compositional Generalization in Continual Few-Shot Learning** (NeurIPS 2026 Main Track, [arXiv:2605.11710](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11710)).
- **MIST: Reliable Streaming Decision Trees for Online Class-Incremental Learning via McDiarmid Bound** (NeurIPS 2026 Main Track, [arXiv:2605.11617](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.11617)).
- **Visual Robustness and Neural Alignment in a Shared Foraging Task: The Mouse vs. AI Benchmark** (NeurIPS 2026 Evaluations and Datasets Track).

## What You Will Gain

- A weekly 1-on-1 with a mentor who has published at venues such as NeurIPS.
- GPU server access for projects that need it.
- Hands-on practice in the full research cycle: question, method, experiments, LaTeX writing and peer review.
- Feedback on applications for graduate study or R&D jobs. The lab does not promise papers, authorship, scholarships, PhD places or jobs. Authorship follows real contribution.

## 4-Round Recruitment Process

1. **Round 1: Application & Research CV:** Submit academic background, coursework, programming experience, and research statement via the official form. No prior publication is required.
2. **Round 2: Basic AI & Machine Learning Assessment:** 30-minute online assessment covering core ML concepts, baseline models, metric selection, and data leakage. Open-book and AI tools are permitted with proper attribution.
3. **Round 3: Structured Research & Culture Interview:** 35 to 45 minute conversational interview about course projects, problem-solving mindset, collaborative dynamics, and research goals.
4. **Round 4: Mini Research Proposal:** Maximum 2-page PDF proposal on a given real-world question (about 3 hours of work, due within 5 days). No model training or empirical results required. The focus is on problem formulation and sound experimental design. The round concludes with a 10-minute presentation and a 10-minute question-and-answer session.
